clinician.final_diagnosis: The patient was diagnosed with subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord and polyneuropathy secondary to concomitant nitrous oxide abuse and autoimmune atrophic gastritis.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 30s presented with lower extremity sensory changes, weakness, and falls. Initial workup revealed functional vitamin B12 deficiency (elevated methylmalonic acid and homocysteine despite normal B12) and intrinsic factor blocking antibodies. MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine showed patchy T2 hyperintensity in the dorsal cord, consistent with subacute combined degeneration. Gastric biopsy indicated chronic inflammation, supporting atrophic gastritis. The patient also had a history of chronic nitrous oxide abuse.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with neurological symptoms including patchy numbness/paresthesias, weakness, difficulty walking, falls, absent vibratory sense, impaired proprioception, diminished two-point discrimination, decreased pinprick sensation, wide-based stance, positive Romberg sign, absent lower extremity reflexes, and no plantar response.
History of daily use of 450 nitrous oxide canisters for 4–5 months.
Elevated methylmalonic acid (5.86 µmol/L) and homocysteine levels (32 µmol/L) despite a normal vitamin B12 level (672 pg/mL), indicating functional B12 deficiency.
Presence of intrinsic factor blocking antibodies.

MRI of the spinal cord revealed patchy hyperintense T2 signal abnormality without enhancement in the dorsal aspect of the cervical and thoracic cord (C3 to T9-T10), consistent with subacute combined degeneration.
Gastric biopsy showed chronic inflammation and reactive changes in the antral and oxyntic mucosa, supporting atrophic gastritis.

remaining_uncertainties: Objective evidence for polyneuropathy (NCS/EMG results were not reported).
